candidates.label: Mantle cell lymphoma, stage IV (involving right cavernous sinus, left pleura, mediastinal lymph nodes)
missing_or_uncertain: CD23 and cyclin D1 status to confirm mantle cell lymphoma

candidates.label: Chronic lymphocytic leukemia/small lymphocytic lymphoma (CLL/SLL) with extranodal involvement (cavernous sinus, pleura)
Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, CD5+ variant, with involvement of cavernous sinus and pleura
Metastatic prostate adenocarcinoma to cavernous sinus and pleura
Tolosa-Hunt syndrome (idiopathic granulomatous inflammation of cavernous sinus)

response.rationale: The biopsy of pleural thickening showing CD5+ CD10− B-cell lymphoma strongly suggests a B-cell lymphoma, with mantle cell lymphoma being the most common CD5+ CD10− subtype. The cavernous sinus involvement and systemic lymphadenopathy indicate stage IV disease. CLL/SLL is less likely given the aggressive presentation and extranodal masses. Metastatic prostate cancer and Tolosa-Hunt syndrome are contradicted by the B-cell biopsy and unremarkable inflammatory markers.
